note: MessageBoard: post() updates a ByteString state field (no sig); burn() verifies real checkSig(owner). Real checkPreimage continuation.

spends.note: owner burn: real checkSig(alice) passes. burn(sig) only asserts checkSig — it does NOT touch `message` — so the continuation must PRESERVE the constructor value 0x00. This expectation used to read "0x" (empty), which was the deep-review C9 bug recorded as if it were correct behaviour: the SDK encoded a 1-byte 0x00 ByteString as OP_0, and OP_0 pushes the EMPTY array, so the state round-tripped 0x00 -> '' and a byte of on-chain state was silently destroyed. With C9/S1 fixed (1-byte 0x00 now encodes as the direct push 01 00, matching the compiler's encodePushBytesHex) the value survives, and this witness records the true on-chain state.
